data.title: Data & privacy
data.description: Spent runs locally. Your credentials are encrypted at rest and never leave your machine.
data.showBrowserHint: Opens a visible Chromium window so you can watch the scrape happen (useful for debugging or solving 2FA / captcha challenges). Also enables verbose scraper logs in your dev terminal.
data.browserVisibleSaved: Browser will be visible on next sync
data.storageCardDescription: Bank credentials and your Claude API key are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. The encryption key lives at data/.encryption-key on your machine (gitignored) and is auto-generated on first run. All transaction data lives in data/spent.db. To reset everything, stop the dev server and delete the data/ directory.
data.excludedDescription: Merchants whose future transactions are automatically excluded from all spending totals. Excluded transactions still appear in the list, faded.
data.dangerDescription: Wipes every synced transaction, sync run, and merchant-memory entry. Your bank credentials, AI settings, budgets, and categories stay put. Use this to start over from a clean slate. Cannot be undone.
data.confirmKeeps: Kept: bank credentials, AI configuration, budgets, categories.

enroll.twoFactorLabel: Also ask for a code from my phone
enroll.twoFactorHint: An authenticator app shows a 6-digit code to type at each sign-in, so a password alone isn't enough. Recommended when Spent can be reached from the internet. You can change this later in Settings, Security.

signIn.codeHint: Open your authenticator app and type the 6-digit code for Spent.
signIn.recoveryHint: Type one of your recovery codes. Each one works once.

screen.signInHint: Your name and password, and a code from your authenticator app if you set one up.
screen.createHint: This Spent is set to require sign-in. Choose a name and password before anything else.
screen.usedRecovery: Signed in with a recovery code. You have {count, plural, =0 {no codes} one {# code} other {# codes}} left. Make new ones in Settings, Security.
screen.lockedOut: Lost your phone and your recovery codes? Whoever runs this server can turn sign-in off with npm run auth:reset.

settings.title: Security
settings.description: Sign-in with a password, and if you like a code from an authenticator app, for when Spent can be reached from other devices or the internet.
settings.offHint: Anyone who can open this address can see and change everything. That's fine on your own computer. Turn sign-in on before you put Spent behind a domain or open it to your network.
settings.enrollHint: You'll sign in with a name and a password. You can also ask for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone.
settings.turnedOn: Sign-in is on. This browser is signed in.
settings.recoveryHint: Each code signs you in once if your phone isn't available.
settings.recoveryLeft: {count, plural, =0 {No codes left} one {# code left} other {# codes left}}
settings.recoveryConfirmHint: Type a code from your authenticator app. Your current recovery codes stop working.
settings.recoveryShownOnce: Save these now. They won't be shown again.
settings.sessionsHint: Each browser stays signed in for 30 days after it was last used.
settings.signedOutOthers: {count, plural, =0 {No other browsers were signed in.} one {Signed out # browser.} other {Signed out # browsers.}}
settings.offCardHint: Removes the password, the authenticator link and the recovery codes, and signs every browser out.
settings.turnOffConfirmHint: Confirm with your password and a code from your authenticator app.
settings.domainHint: A few things to know before Spent is reachable from outside this computer.
settings.domainHttps: Serve it over HTTPS (a reverse proxy such as Caddy, Traefik or nginx). Sign-in cookies are marked secure when the request arrives over HTTPS.
settings.domainRequired: Set SPENT_AUTH_REQUIRED=1 on the server so a fresh install asks for a sign-in before anything else, even before setup.
settings.domainReset: Locked out? On the server, run
settings.offCardSharing: Everyone you shared with loses access too.
settings.renameHint: The name you type when you sign in. Your password, authenticator app and recovery codes stay the same.
settings.renameConfirmHint: Pick a new name and confirm with your password. It has to be one nobody else here uses.
settings.twoFactorOnHint: Each sign-in also asks for a 6-digit code from the app on your phone.
settings.twoFactorOffHint: Only your password protects this account. Add an authenticator app so a stolen password isn't enough.
settings.twoFactorAddHint: Confirm with your password, then connect the app on your phone.
settings.twoFactorRemoveHint: Confirm with your password and a code from the app. After this your password alone signs you in, and your recovery codes stop working.
settings.twoFactorRemoved: The authenticator app is off. Your password alone signs you in.

requests.ownerHint: People you shared with think these belong in another category. Nothing changes until you approve.
requests.approvedToast: {count, plural, one {Suggestion approved} other {# suggestions approved}}
requests.declinedToast: {count, plural, one {Suggestion declined} other {# suggestions declined}}
requests.sentToast: Suggested {category}. {owner} will see it and decide.

viewer.badgeHint: You can look around and suggest categories. Changes are up to the owner.
viewer.badgeHintNamed: This is {owner}'s spending. You can look around and suggest categories; {owner} decides.
viewer.accountHint: You have view-only access. You can suggest a category for any transaction, and the owner approves it.
viewer.accountHintNamed: {owner} shared their spending with you to view. You can suggest a category for any transaction, and {owner} approves it.
viewer.pageDescription: Your sign-in, recovery codes and the browsers you're signed in on.

invite.title: {owner} shared their spending with you
invite.hint: Create your own sign-in to view it. You'll see everything shared and can suggest categories, but not change anything.
invite.footer: Only {owner} can change what you see or remove your access.
invite.goneHint: Invite links work once and expire after a week. Ask for a new one.
invite.signedInHint: This browser is signed in as {name}. Sign out to join with this invite.

settings.title: Sharing
settings.description: Let someone see your spending without being able to change it. They can suggest a better category for a transaction, and you approve it.
settings.needsSignInHint: Everyone gets their own sign-in, so Spent can tell you apart and keep them view-only.
settings.inviteHint: Create a link and send it to them. They choose their own name, password and authenticator app.
settings.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the link and copy it.
settings.linkNote: It works once, for {days} days. Send it privately: whoever opens it first gets access. This link won't be shown again.
settings.peopleHint: Tap a workspace to share or stop sharing it.
settings.peopleEmpty: No one yet. Create an invite link above.
settings.nothingShared: Nothing is shared with them right now.
settings.removeHint: Their sign-in is deleted and they're signed out everywhere. Their open suggestions stay for you to decide. You can invite them again later.
settings.openHint: Not used yet. Revoke one if it went to the wrong person.
settings.canSee: See everything in the workspaces you share: transactions, budgets, insights and charts.
settings.canSuggest: Suggest a category for a transaction. It shows up on your Home and Transactions pages to approve or decline.
settings.cannot: They can't sync, edit, set budgets, see your bank logins or open Settings.
settings.renameHint: They sign in with the new name from now on. Their password and authenticator app stay the same, so let them know.
